negative_reviews.author: Alzahraa Nagi Ali Al-Mughrbi
negative_reviews.text:
Not the best and NOT allergen friendly

The prices are a lot plus a service fee especially seeing as no waiter came to use for 20 mins despite the place not being crowded.
And not as allergen friendly as promised especially with nuts. For a restaurant that claims to be nut free MOST of the food was labelled by an employee (who knew alarmingly little about it herself) as “may contain nuts”. Apparently they don’t even know what’s in their own pastes and admit they might have nuts but can’t confirm it be liable or prevent cross contamination which is BS.

Also there’s a glitch in their app that gives £5 coupon and says it’s viable for two weeks but isn’t accepted after 29/10 so be careful for that

negative_reviews.author: Berke
negative_reviews.text:
I had really high expectations coming here but when I tried the Ramen with meat... I had the worst experience. I think it was mixed with some fish from other spoons because I tasted fish in my ramen.
Other than the horrible smell of the ramen, the restaurant is top tear looking but really loud inside. Every other minute the waitresses play the gong and its annoying after the tenth...

deliveroo.source: sales + orders: Deliveroo Tax Invoice PDF (Total Order Value), issued 02/11/2026 + ops from Weekly Summary sheet

issues: Sales and covers dropped on Friday and Sunday after the £5 ramen promotion ended, while spend per head rose by about £3 back to the normal £22 to £24 (England KPI meeting 03/11).
Wages were reported as on track (England KPI meeting 03/11).
Loyalty member bills dropped sharply after the £5 ramen ended, and few customers have used the app to collect points since Thursday (England KPI meeting 03/11).
Deliveroo was amber: rating and prep time slipped, and rider wait was hit by a Wednesday lunchtime queue and several large delivery orders (England KPI meeting 03/11).

Google reviews: one complained the steak ramen tasted fishy (possibly the wakame), a 3 star said the steak ramen does not blend well, and an allergy complaint came from a misunderstanding of 'may contain' wording, which the site checked on CCTV (England KPI meeting 03/11).
Staffing: BOH hired two sushi chefs with a kitchen assistant joining this week, and FOH has made one new hire (England KPI meeting 03/11).
The guest Wi-Fi registration page does not pop up even though devices connect to the signal, and rebooting has not fixed it (England KPI meeting 03/11).
Five second greetings, table check backs and immediate delivery bag handovers are being followed (England KPI meeting 03/11).
The fish supplier asked for a back door key for delayed deliveries; Inka said a key for the special lock needs landlord authorisation and costs over £200 (England KPI meeting 03/11).
Christmas leaflets have been collected and allergy sheets are being printed (England KPI meeting 03/11).
Inka said Deliveroo improvements for Manchester will wait until the other sites reach green (England KPI meeting 03/11).
actions: Retrain the team member involved in the allergy complaint on the allergy protocol and 'may contain' wording - Owner: Manchester GM (10/11/2026)
Enter current staff status in the dashboard staff column - Owner: Manchester GM (10/11/2026)
Send a screenshot of the guest Wi-Fi registration page error to Inka - Owner: Manchester GM (10/11/2026)
Find and send an Amazon link for small shelves by the back door for delivery bags - Owner: Manchester GM (10/11/2026)
Email the guest Wi-Fi contact about the registration error, copying Maki Manchester - Owner: Inka Cheung (10/11/2026)
Try to get an authorised back door key for Manchester from the landlord - Owner: Inka Cheung (10/11/2026)
